pages.text: "Mom, who's that zebra?" Moya hid behind her legs. A zebra with white fur on her back walked slowly along the red dirt path. Moya wanted to stay beside Mom.
Mom stepped forward happily. "Grandma! She walked a long way from a distant herd." Grandma held out her muzzle. "You've grown so much!" Moya shyly backed away. "Hello..." came a tiny voice.
Grandma smelled different. Her stripes were different, too, and soft white fur covered her back. Moya tapped at dirt in the acacia shade. "I like being with Mom... When will Grandma leave?"
Grandma brought a yellow fruit in her mouth. "Try this, little one. I carried it on my way here." Moya bit in. Sweet juice spread through their mouth. "...It's good."
Grandma took Moya to the reeds. "A game from when I was little?" She tapped a reed with her muzzle. White seeds floated up. Moya tapped, too. "Like clouds!" For the first time, Moya smiled.
Mom whispered, "Grandma walked all that way to see you. She carried that fruit from far away, too." Moya looked at Grandma's dusty hooves. "All that way... for me?" Their heart stirred.
Grandma slowly lay on the grass. "Climb onto my back." Moya hopped up. Her white fur was the softest, warmest thing in the world. "A ride on Grandma's back!" Moya's neck straightened.
At sunset, the herd lay in a circle. Moya snuggled beside Grandma's tummy. She told stories of her distant herd. "Hippos live at our waterhole..." Moya laughed. Grandma wasn't strange anymore.

Morning came, and Grandma had to return. Moya recited the steps. "One, come out from behind Mom! Two, share a bite! Three, snuggle onto your back!" "Come again, Grandma! I'll miss you!" Moya sniffled.
Grandma nuzzled Moya's neck for a long time. Mom hugged them with her neck. "You love Grandma now!" Eating and playing together had turned a stranger into someone dear. A ride on Grandma's back!
